about: Signed visitor tokens and the verdict every verifier must give each: the TypeScript check in packages/common and the Python check in python/lb-common, which the Django, Flask and Node systems use. Made by packages/common/scripts/visitor-token-corpus.ts; do not edit by hand.

rules.T1: A token is at most 2048 characters.
rules.T2: A token is three segments of letters, digits, "-" and "_", none empty, joined by dots: no padding, no spaces, nothing else.
rules.T3: Each segment is canonical base64url: it decodes, and encodes back to the same text.
rules.T4: The header is a UTF-8 JSON object with no byte order mark, whose members are strings, numbers, booleans or null; "alg" is exactly "EdDSA"; there is no "crit" member.
rules.T5: The signature is 64 bytes and verifies, as Ed25519 (RFC 8032, so with S reduced) with the site's key, over the first two segments as written.
rules.T6: The claims are a UTF-8 JSON object with no byte order mark, whose members are strings, numbers, booleans or null, except "aud", which may be a list of strings; "iss", "aud", "sub", "iat" and "exp" are all there.
rules.T8: "aud" is the system's name, as a string or in a list that holds nothing but strings.
rules.T9: "iat", "exp" and "nbf" (when there) are JSON numbers with a whole value no bigger than 2^53 - 1: 1.0 and 1e9 are whole; 1.5, strings, booleans, null and lists are not.
rules.T11: With 30 seconds of leeway, "exp" is later than now - 30, and "iat" and "nbf" are no later than now + 30.
rules.T13: Any other member is ignored, as long as its value is a string, number, boolean or null.
rules.H1: An Authorization header is stripped of leading and trailing spaces and tabs, and of nothing else.
rules.H2: What is left is "Bearer" in any case, one or more spaces, and a token (T1 to T13), with nothing after it.
rules.K1: The site's key is the unpadded, canonical base64url of exactly 32 bytes.
